1kqwjh0: You already know that “si” is followed by the present. In real situations, the result tells you what kind of sentence it is. With the future, you make a prediction or take a decision now: “Si el río está alto, tomaremos otra lancha”. With the present, you present a plan already agreed: “Si llueve, salimos a las diez” (the group has already decided it).
vl5gf0: When both parts are in the present and the situation repeats, it is a rule or a habit: “Si encuentras un nido, avisas al guardaparques”. For plan B, use “si no” (with no pause between “si” and “no”) or “en ese caso”: “Si el autobús llega a tiempo, comemos en Cariari; si no, comemos en la lancha”.
wbkhc5: Even if you talk about the future, “si” is followed by the present.
jbx1v6: For plan B you write “si no”, as two words. “Sino” means “but rather”.
q2h0y9: A very natural way of giving advice is to say what you would do: “Yo llevaría botas de goma”, “Yo no dejaría la mochila en la playa”. The other person decides; you only suggest. It sounds softer than the imperative (“Lleva botas”) and less direct than “tienes que”.
1c32zyj: You can combine it with a real condition to make a friendly suggestion: “Si tienes tiempo, podrías ayudarnos con los nidos”, “Si vas al mercado, yo compraría frutas para el viaje”. For a compulsory rule, on the other hand, use the present, “tener que” or the imperative.
1kzva6s: Ask yourself: who decides? If the other person decides, advise with “yo + conditional”; if it is a rule, use the present or the imperative.

18bpum8: “Por”, “para” and “pa’”: little prepositions in fast speech
yie44m: “Por” and “para” are unstressed words: they have no stress and they stick to the next word (“porla mañana”, “parael lunes”). That is why they are easy to miss. Pay attention to the vowel: “por” has a single syllable with “o”; “para” has two syllables with “a”.
h4o8mi: In the informal speech of many countries, Costa Rica included, “para” is reduced to “pa’”: “pa’ la playa”, “pa’ que veas”. It is normal in a conversation between friends, but it is not written that way in a formal text. When you speak, pronounce “para” in full and mark the soft final r of “por”.
ypy7ab: The form “pa’” is spoken. In texts always write “para”, and remember that “si no” (condition) is written as two words and “sino” (but rather) as one.

zscqa7: Welcome to Arena Viva. Thank you for choosing us for your holiday: your work over these weeks is very important for the green turtles, which come to this beach between July and October to lay their eggs. nygum7: What is compulsory: if you are on shift, you arrive at the hut ten minutes early and sign the attendance sheet. 9mydvr: The advice: we would have a nap on patrol days, because the nights are long. We wouldn’t spend a lot in the village on the first day either: there are things for half the price at the Thursday market.
